Circular infinite quantum well (Em,j​=ℏ2j∣m∣,j2​/(2μa2))

Words: 69
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A particle confined by a Dirichlet boundary condition to a disc of radius a has angular functions eimϕ, m∈Z, and regular radial Bessel functions of the first kind J∣m∣​(kr). Their boundary zeros give the displayed energies. The ground state belongs to m=0: nonzero angular modes add a nonnegative centrifugal term to the kinetic-energy form. At the origin exclude the singular radial solution, rather than accepting every square-integrable logarithmic function as a physical eigenstate.

Hegerfeldt theorem

Words: 89
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Let H be a self-adjoint Hamiltonian bounded below, A a bounded positive operator and pA​(t)=⟨e−iHtψ,Ae−iHtψ⟩. The Hegerfeldt theorem states that either pA​(t) vanishes identically or it is nonzero for almost every real time. In particular, vanishing throughout an open interval forces identically vanishing. The proof uses analytic continuation of A1/2e−iHtψ into the lower half-plane. Applied to an assumed sharp localization effect, this obstructs strict finite-speed localization for positive-energy one-particle dynamics. It does not identify a controllable superluminal signal: the localization observables and admissible local preparation procedures need separate analysis.

Rotating-wave approximation

Words: 84
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
After expressing a driven Quantum Hamiltonian in a suitable interaction or rotating frame, discard terms oscillating rapidly compared with the retained dynamics. Near a selected transition, this leaves resonant terms that accumulate coherently while counter-rotating terms average out to leading order. The drive strength and detuning must be small relative to the discarded oscillation frequencies over the intended regime; strong driving can require the neglected frequency shifts and corrections. The approximation supports resonant quantum control, but it is not exact merely because the carrier is tuned to resonance.

Quantum rotor (H=ℓ2/(2I),En​=ℏ2n2/(2I))

Words: 383 Articles: 7
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A quantum coordinate on a circle with kinetic Hamiltonian ℓ2/(2I). Periodic wavefunctions have angular momentum ℏn and energy ℏ2n2/(2I) for integer n. Its thermal trace has both a momentum-eigenstate sum and a topological winding-path representation. Twisted boundary conditions or flux would modify this spectrum and are separate models.

Real-time winding representation of a quantum rotor kernel (K=I/(2πiℏT)​∑m​eiI(Δ+2πm)2/(2ℏT))

Words: 69
Quantum rotor OurBigBook.com
The quantum rotor with angle period 2π has both the spectral kernel (2π)−1∑n​einΔ−iℏn2T/(2I) and the displayed winding representation. The Poisson summation formula converts one into the other by a Gaussian integral. Each winding sector has a constant-velocity classical path and action I(Δ+2πm)2/(2T). Quadratic fluctuations give the same prefactor in every sector, so this is exact. Real time is understood by T→T−i0, which fixes the square-root branch and convergence prescription.

Coupled quantum rotor chain (H=∑n​[ℓn2​/(2I)−Jcos(ϕn+1​−ϕn​)])

Words: 145 Articles: 2
Quantum rotor OurBigBook.com
A chain with local rotor inertia and a phase-locking interaction −Jcos(ϕn+1​−ϕn​). Its smooth-phase limit is an elastic phase field with inertia I and stiffness J. Compact winding and phase-slip processes remain part of the full model even when absent from the Gaussian smooth-sector approximation.

Harmonic phase mode of a quantum rotor chain (ω(q)=2J/I​∣sin(q/2)∣)

Words: 48
Coupled quantum rotor chain OurBigBook.com
Expanding the cosine gives a wave equation Iϕtt​=Jϕxx​ and a gapless phase mode with physical frequency J/I​∣q∣. The exact harmonic lattice frequency is 2J/I​∣sin(q/2)∣. It resembles superfluid sound. In one dimension, Gaussian phase fluctuations and possible compact phase slips require care before inferring true long-range order from this branch.

Imaginary-time normalization for a coupled rotor chain (S=∫dτdx[Iϕ˙​2/(2ℏ2)+Jϕx2​/2])

Words: 51
Coupled quantum rotor chain OurBigBook.com
When imaginary time is divided by ℏ and ranges from zero to β, integrating rotor momenta gives Iϕ˙​2/(2ℏ2) but leaves the potential stiffness term J(∂x​ϕ)2/2. Factoring 1/ℏ2 out of both terms requires spatial coefficient ℏ2J inside the bracket. Setting ℏ=1 hides this distinction, but restoring units must preserve it.

Rotor winding-sector path integral (ϕ(β)−ϕ(0)=2πm)

Words: 118 Articles: 2
Quantum rotor OurBigBook.com
The thermal rotor path integral traces paths closed modulo 2π. Lift them to the line and sum endpoints differing by 2πm. In inverse-energy time 0<τ<β, the kinetic exponent is I∫ϕ˙​2dτ/(2ℏ2). Integer m counts trajectory windings, not angular-momentum eigenstates.

Momentum-winding duality of the quantum rotor (∑n​e−an2=π/a​∑m​e−π2m2/a)

Words: 35
Rotor winding-sector path integral OurBigBook.com
Poisson resummation relates the momentum sum ∑n​e−βℏ2n2/(2I) to the winding sum 2πI/(βℏ2)​∑m​e−2π2Im2/(βℏ2). Gaussian Fourier transformation proves equality, including the prefactor. The momentum form converges rapidly at low temperature and the winding form at high temperature.

Rotor return-kernel fluctuation prefactor (Z0​=I/(2πℏ2β)​)

Words: 42
Rotor winding-sector path integral OurBigBook.com
Writing ϕ=ϕ0​+2πmτ/β+η with endpoint-fixed η separates winding action and Gaussian fluctuations. The latter give the free return kernel on the lifted line, Z0​=I/(2πℏ2β)​. The starting-angle integral supplies 2π. Zero winding is not the same as the zero-momentum ground-state sector.

Semiclassical quantization (I/ℏ≫1)

Words: 99 Articles: 1
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Semiclassical quantization uses classical trajectories and actions to approximate quantum states in a regime where relevant actions are large compared with ℏ. Phase consistency on a periodic orbit leads to Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization. Soliton collective coordinates can be quantized this way, while fluctuations supply additional corrections to the leading classical mass.

Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization (∮pdq=2πℏ(N+μ/4))

Words: 53
Semiclassical quantization OurBigBook.com
Single-valued semiclassical phase on a closed classical orbit quantizes its action, with Maslov index μ accounting for turning-point phase corrections. Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
When a Hamiltonian operator changes instantaneously by a finite potential step, the quantum state is continuous across the switching time. Its coefficients in the new energy eigenbasis are its overlaps with those eigenstates; the Born rule gives their squared moduli as probabilities. The state need not remain an energy eigenstate of the new Hamiltonian.

If the endpoints change instantaneously to ±ηa, with η>1, the sudden approximation leaves the wave function unchanged, extended by zero outside the old well. Its overlap with the new normalized ground state (ηa)−1/2cos(πx/(2ηa)) is 4η3/2cos(π/(2η))/[π(η2−1)]. The Born rule squares this probability amplitude; for η=2 the result is 64/(9π2), and the limit as η↓1 is 1.

Their canonical commutation relations give the photon creation and annihilation operators. Covariant Gupta-Bleuler quantization instead retains auxiliary polarization modes and selects the same physical state space by a subsidiary condition and null-state quotient.

Photon OurBigBook.com
Two first-class constraints in Maxwell theory remove four phase-space variables from the eight variables of a four-component potential and its momenta. Photon OurBigBook.com
Photon absorption removes a photon and transfers its energy and momentum to matter. It contributes a negative photon-number collision source. It differs from Compton scattering, which redistributes a photon's energy and direction while preserving the count. The integrated source can vanish if photon emission and absorption balance.

Photon OurBigBook.com
Photon emission creates a photon, for example in bremsstrahlung or the decay of an excited material state. For distinguishable particles with one-particle Hilbert spaces Hi​, the multiparticle state space is ⨂i​Hi​. A product state is a tensor product of one-particle states, while a general state is a linear combination of product states.

Particle exchange operator (P12​)

Multiparticle quantum state OurBigBook.com
For two particles, the exchange operator sends ∣α⟩⊗∣β⟩ to ∣β⟩⊗∣α⟩. It has eigenvalues +1 on symmetric states and −1 on antisymmetric states.
Indistinguishable particles

Particle exchange operator OurBigBook.com
Physical states of identical particles have definite symmetry under every particle exchange operator: symmetric for bosons and antisymmetric for fermions.
Boson
Words: 122 Articles: 2
Indistinguishable particles OurBigBook.com
Bosons are identical particles whose total multiparticle state is symmetric under exchange. In three-dimensional relativistic quantum theory they have integer spin.
Bosonic exchange symmetry
Words: 101 Articles: 1
Boson OurBigBook.com
Bosonic exchange symmetry is the symmetric exchange statistics of identical bosons. Commuting creation operators build the symmetric bosonic Fock space; a normalized one-particle mode has occupation states (a†)n∣0⟩/n!​ for every nonnegative integer n. At thermal equilibrium this symmetry leads to Bose-Einstein statistics and the Bose-Einstein distribution. Exchange symmetry itself does not require thermal equilibrium.
Bosonic statistics from commuting creation operators ([ap†​,aq†​]=0)
Words: 56
Bosonic exchange symmetry OurBigBook.com
Commuting creation operators make multiparticle states invariant under exchange of their labels. With [a,a†]=1, the normalized number states (a†)r∣0⟩/r!​ exist for all r≥0, giving unrestricted bosonic occupation numbers. The single-mode thermal sum is Z=∑r≥0​e−βEr=(1−e−βE)−1 and the mean occupation is (eβE−1)−1. Thus the exchange symmetry and the Bose-Einstein distribution are two expressions of the same bosonic algebra.
Fermion
Words: 134 Articles: 3
Indistinguishable particles OurBigBook.com
Fermions are identical particles whose total multiparticle state is antisymmetric under exchange. In three-dimensional relativistic quantum theory they have half-integer spin.
Fermi-Dirac statistics
Words: 55
Fermion OurBigBook.com
The antisymmetric exchange statistics of identical fermions. Interchanging two one-particle labels reverses the total state, and fermionic creation operators anticommute. Occupation of a one-particle mode is therefore zero or one, giving the Pauli exclusion principle; thermal equilibrium leads to the Fermi-Dirac distribution. Color, flavor, spin and orbital factors must together have the required antisymmetry, even if one factor is symmetric.
Exchange symmetry of two identical spin-one-half fermions
Words: 32
Fermion OurBigBook.com
For two identical spin-one-half fermions with no additional antisymmetric internal factor, the antisymmetric spin-one-half singlet state combines with an even-ℓ symmetric orbital state, while the symmetric spin-one-half triplet state combines with an odd-ℓ antisymmetric orbital state.
Pauli exclusion principle
Words: 26
Fermion OurBigBook.com
No two identical fermions may occupy the same one-particle quantum state. At zero temperature, noninteracting fermions fill the available one-particle states in increasing order of energy.
Spin-statistics theorem
Words: 29
Indistinguishable particles OurBigBook.com
The spin-statistics theorem associates integer-spin particles with bosonic exchange symmetry and half-integer-spin particles with fermionic exchange symmetry in relativistic quantum field theory under the standard locality and positivity assumptions.
Two identical spin-one bosons
Words: 83 Articles: 1
Indistinguishable particles OurBigBook.com
For two spin-one particles, the spin tensor product has a six-dimensional symmetric subspace and a three-dimensional antisymmetric subspace. A symmetric spatial state combines with symmetric spin, while an antisymmetric spatial state combines with antisymmetric spin, so that the total bosonic state remains symmetric.

gN​=⎩⎨⎧​29​N+6,29​(N+1),​N even,N odd.​

Each unequal orbital pair contributes six symmetric-spin states and three antisymmetric-spin states; an equal orbital pair exists only for even N and contributes six states.

Time-dependent perturbation theory

Words: 156 Articles: 3
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Expanding a state in unperturbed energy eigenstates with their free phases converts the time-dependent Schrodinger equation into coupled equations for slowly varying amplitudes. To first order, the perturbation on the right-hand side acts on the initial unperturbed state.
This is the time-dependent branch of perturbation theory; its corrections describe transition amplitudes.

Words: 73 Articles: 1
Time-dependent perturbation theory OurBigBook.com
In the long-wavelength approximation, a particle of charge q in a spatially uniform electric field has perturbation
Δ(t)=−qE(t)⋅r.
(109)
Its transition amplitudes are controlled by matrix elements of the position operator.

Electric-dipole selection rule

Words: 41
Electric-dipole interaction OurBigBook.com
Because the position operator has odd parity, an electric-dipole matrix element vanishes between states of the same parity. For orbital-angular-momentum eigenstates, the full rule is Δℓ=±1 and Δm=0,±1, with the field polarization selecting the allowed change in m.

Ω(k)/2sin(Ω(k)t/2)​.

(Ω/2)2sin2(Ωt/2)​⟶2πtδ(Ω)

selects energy-conserving continuum states and produces a transition probability linear in time.

Time-independent perturbation theory

Words: 265 Articles: 8
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Time-independent perturbation theory expands the eigenvalues and eigenstates of H0​+V in powers of a small perturbation V.
This is the stationary branch of perturbation theory.

Hellmann–Feynman theorem (E′(λ)=⟨ψ,H′(λ)ψ⟩)

Words: 49
Time-independent perturbation theory OurBigBook.com
For a differentiable normalized eigenstate of a differentiable self-adjoint Hamiltonian, differentiate Hψ=Eψ and pair with ψ. The terms involving ψ′ cancel because H is self-adjoint, leaving the stated formula. It turns energy derivatives into observable expectations. A smoothly chosen eigenbranch and suitable operator-domain regularity are required, particularly at degeneracies or crossings.

Bright and dark state reduction of a star-coupled Hamiltonian

Words: 68
Time-independent perturbation theory OurBigBook.com
Suppose one state ∣0⟩ couples to degenerate states ∣1⟩,…,∣m⟩ with amplitudes v1​,…,vm​, while the degenerate states do not couple to each other. The normalized bright state proportional to ∑j​vj​∣j⟩ is the only combination coupled to ∣0⟩. Every orthogonal combination is a dark state and remains an exact eigenstate at the degenerate energy. The remaining spectrum comes from a two-dimensional Hamiltonian whose off-diagonal entry is (∑j​∣vj​∣2)1/2.

Pauli X eigenstate

Words: 26
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
The Pauli X eigenstates are (∣0⟩±∣1⟩)/2​ with eigenvalues ±1.
These are the eigenvectors of one Pauli matrix, not an alternative name for the whole matrix family.

Rectangular potential barrier

Words: 36
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
A rectangular potential barrier has a constant elevated potential over a finite interval and a lower constant potential outside it. Matching wavefunctions and derivatives at the interval endpoints gives its reflection and transmission amplitudes. It is a special potential barrier.

Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)

Words: 18
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
Perturbation theory expands a quantum problem around a solvable Hamiltonian. Time-independent perturbation theory expands stationary energies and eigenstates; time-dependent perturbation theory expands dynamical amplitudes and transitions.

Hartree equations

Words: 33
Quantum mechanics OurBigBook.com
The Hartree equations are self-consistent one-particle equations obtained by approximating a many-body wave function by a tensor product of orbital wave functions. Each orbital sees the potential averaged over the other particles' probability densities; attractive Newtonian mean-field variants include the Gravitational Hartree equation.
